source_text: So, the "I/me" paragraphs give a "point of view" character (McCloud on comics)... not saying we should use comic sans for that section but it's a distinct logical "box" from the we sections that follow.  Contact is on the about page, which I think is OK.  My point about LLMs is that they are great but not sufficient for the kinds of thing that people actually need to do high-quality technical work... I don't think that's terribly contentious (the 2019 part could go).  As for "first engagement" the point is really that we've done the 0th engagement ourselves, and that's what the contents of the "about" page illustrate.  So "to do the kind of work we're interested in we had to build a system in which agents could chat with each other and self organise work, in which you could search the entire history using free-text search or graph queries, in which you could monitor the flow of work transparently.  We can build something to suit the requirements of your organisation."  But yeah, in reality, "building the first engagement" might take some more work, e.g., connecting Jira to agent mission or whatnot.  Meanwhile I can keep working on the War Machine & Rob and I can keep working on the Lean4 parser ... those could provide additional proofs of concept or tooling but we're not ready to advertise them on a public website yet.

reply_text:
㊥ (the index page, after your points) I take back two of my four criticisms and have redrafted the other two sections with your wording. One check against the about page: of the three capabilities in your "0th engagement" sentence, the about page clearly shows only the third, monitoring.

🈹 (voice and contact) I withdraw the point about "I" and "we": as a point-of-view box followed by the company's voice, it is a design choice and it reads that way once named. I also withdraw the contact point. One small thing the box lacks is a name. The reader meets "I" and "Me running agents like a boss" but does not learn who is speaking until the about page, so a signature under the box would give the character an identity.

🈹 (my reason against the slogan) I said the Philip K. Dick reference was a stray bad association. The about page opens with a Dick quotation, so he is a house reference and that reason is weaker than I made it. Your own reason stands: clients control the system, we do not remember for them.

㊭ (the harness section, without 2019) Under "We're building an agentic harness for knowledge work":

> Language models are very good, and on their own they are not enough for high-quality technical work. Decades of research on learning and on mapping knowledge domains, consulting with clients on strategic plans, and years of work with online communities have given us methods for guiding and governing AI-assisted work, based on the way collective intelligence works.

㊭ (the 0th engagement, in your words) Directly after it, replacing "Click through for more information":

> To do the kind of work we are interested in, we had to build a system in which agents can talk to each other and organise work among themselves, in which the whole history can be searched by free text or by graph queries, and in which the flow of work can be watched as it happens. We were our own first client, and the about page shows what came of it. We can build something to suit the requirements of your organisation, starting from the tools you already use.

The last clause is mine. It is there for your Jira point: it tells a reader that connecting to their systems is part of the job, without promising a particular integration.

㊩ (what the about page shows) I read the staging copy, which is the same as the live one. It shows the live map of your work, the mission landscape, the harness map, and three offerings (log diagnostic, provenance, controls). That covers "watch the flow of work". It has no figure of agents talking to each other and none of search. The phone screenshot of agent seats is on the index, not the about page. So either the sentence should claim less, or the about page needs two more figures.

㊟ (not advertising the War Machine or the Lean work) Agreed, and nothing I drafted mentions either. The about page's harness caption already says the harness is "based on Active Inference and checked against a formal model in Lean". That is live today, so I only flag it in case you want it toned down.

🈸 (two things still open from my last turn) Shall I put these drafts, with the memory section, into the `futon7a-staging` worktree for you to read in place, uncommitted? And shall I commit the notebook edits and pass the next steps to claude-17?
